note: Where you may not shoot, verbatim from the Mammal Hunting and Trapping Regulations. The 150-yard safety zone is stored with its qualifying clause because the qualification IS the rule: it binds only a person who is not the owner or occupier and lacks their express permission.

records.title: Near a dwelling, building or barn
records.applies_unless: You are the owner, the person in possession of the premises, or you have the express permission of one of them.
records.verbatim: (a) It is unlawful for a person, other than the owner, person in possession of the premises, or a person having the express permission of the owner or person in possession of the premises, while within 150 yards of an occupied dwelling house, residence, or other building, or within 150 yards of a barn or other outbuilding used in connection with an occupied dwelling house, residence, or other building, to either hunt or discharge a firearm or other deadly weapon while hunting. The 150-yard area is a “safety zone.”

citation.source_doc: Fish and Game Commission, Mammal Hunting and Trapping Regulations p.24: 2026 Mammal Booklet v1_Final Draft_published_7.1_.pdf

records.title: Over or across a public road
records.verbatim: (b) It is unlawful for a person to intentionally discharge a firearm or release an arrow or crossbow bolt over or across a public road or other established way open to the public in an unsafe and reckless manner

citation.source_doc: Fish and Game Commission, Mammal Hunting and Trapping Regulations p.24: 2026 Mammal Booklet v1_Final Draft_published_7.1_.pdf

records.title: A loaded rifle or shotgun in a vehicle
records.verbatim: (a) It is unlawful to possess a loaded rifle or shotgun in any vehicle or conveyance or its attachments which is standing on or along or is being driven on or along any public highway or other way open to the public.

citation.source_doc: Fish and Game Commission, Mammal Hunting and Trapping Regulations p.24: 2026 Mammal Booklet v1_Final Draft_published_7.1_.pdf

no_road_setback.statement: These regulations set no minimum distance from a road. What they prohibit is the act: discharging over or across a public road, shooting from or upon one, and carrying a loaded rifle or shotgun in a vehicle on one.
no_road_setback.checked: Every distance printed in the hunting booklets was checked: 150 yards (dwellings), 400 yards (bait), 150 feet (litter near the high-water mark), and several wildlife-area figures. None concerns roads.

penal_code_summary.verbatim: Shoot any firearm from or upon a public road or highway.
penal_code_summary.caveat: The booklet prints this as a one-line summary only. The text it reproduces under that section number is the littering statute, so the operative Penal Code sentence is not in this app.

citation.source_doc: Fish and Game Commission, Mammal Hunting and Trapping Regulations p.5: 2026 Mammal Booklet v1_Final Draft_published_7.1_.pdf

archery_across_road.verbatim: (e) No arrow or crossbow bolt may be released from a bow or crossbow upon or across any highway, road or other way open to vehicular traffic.

citation.source_doc: Fish and Game Commission, Mammal Hunting and Trapping Regulations p.22: 2026 Mammal Booklet v1_Final Draft_published_7.1_.pdf

not_covered: Schools, playgrounds, occupied camps and public buildings — the hunting booklets are silent, so this app is too.
